mainTopic: Did בית שמאי act on their own rulings (עשו)? The גמרא tests several sources and stories, from the תקנה for צרות to רבי עקיבא's אתרוג, שמאי's סוכה, and the trough of יהוא.
overview: The גמרא asks whether בית שמאי actually acted on their own rulings (עשו), especially their view that a צרה may do יבום. First it brings a ברייתא: the חכמים wanted to rule that all צרות do חליצה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asked, 'What shall we do with the earlier צרות?' רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that this worry fits even if בית שמאי never acted. It is about צרות who married others without חליצה, following בית הלל. Next, רבי טרפון's wish to 'marry' his daughter's צרה is reread as 'marry her off,' and the story of רבן גמליאל doing יבום with his daughter's צרה is explained by the fact that she was an אילונית. Then רב משרשיא and מר זוטרא bring stories of action that looks like בית שמאי's view: רבי עקיבא's double tithe on an אתרוג, and שמאי's סוכה over a newborn. Each is answered: רבי עקיבא was unsure what בית הלל held, and onlookers would think שמאי just wanted fresh air. Finally מר זוטרא brings the trough of יהוא, which בית שמאי widened, and the גמרא's answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: The proposed rule for צרות is cut off by a time of trouble
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the proposal that צרות should do חליצה and not יבום, and then says the חכמים could not finish deciding before troubled times came.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Let us make a rule for the co-wives] that they should do חליצה and not יבום. But they did not manage to finish the matter before a time of trouble came.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא the גמרא is quoting finishes the proposed fix: every צרה should do חליצה, never יבום. Then it tells us the vote never happened because troubled times broke out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה is the safe path for everyone. For בית שמאי it frees the צרה to marry, and for בית הלל it does no harm. The proposal was never finalized, and that sets up רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They do חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from the brother-in-law
They marry the brother-in-law (יבום)
A co-wife, here the co-wife of a relative forbidden to the יבם
The time became troubled (a period of danger or upheaval)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that began earlier: 'Come, let us make a תקנה for the צרות.' It is not a new topic.

phrases.english: that they should do חליצה and not do יבום.
They did not manage to finish the matter
before the time became troubled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting just before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים proposed that צרות do חליצה only, but the proposal was never finalized.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asks what to do with the earlier צרות
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל raises a problem: what happens now to the צרות who already acted in the past?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to him: What shall we do with the earlier צרות from now on?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about the צרות from before the new rule. This sets up the גמרא's analysis in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a new rule now could create trouble for women who already acted under the old practice. The גמרא will ask exactly what trouble he had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: What shall we do?
The earlier ones (from before the new rule)
From now on

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מָה נַעֲשֶׂה לָהֶם לַצָּרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת מֵעַתָּה?
phrases.english: What shall we do with the earlier co-wives from now on?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַעֲשֶׂה לָהֶם לַצָּרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Still part of the ברייתא. He reacts to the proposed תקנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adopting the תקנה is complicated by the status of earlier צרות.

steps.title: The question only makes sense if בית שמאי acted on their view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's worry proves בית שמאי really did act (עשו), since otherwise there would be no earlier problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they acted: that is why he said 'What shall we do?' But if you say they did not act, what does 'What shall we do?' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא as proof that בית שמאי did act on their opinion. If צרות really did יבום, there are past marriages and children to worry about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי acted, some צרות married the יבם. A new rule forbidding that would make those unions problematic and could make their children ממזרים, which explains 'What shall we do?' If they never acted, nothing was done that needs fixing, so the question seems empty.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (this side makes sense)
They acted (בית שמאי put their view into practice)
That is why he said
What (is the meaning of)?

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the main pieces of evidence in the סוגיא's big question: whether עשו בית שמאי כדבריהם.

phrases.english: It works well if you say they acted —
phrases.notes: 'They' means בית שמאי, acting on their view that a צרה may do יבום.

phrases.english: that is why he said 'What shall we do?'
But if you say they did not act,
what does 'What shall we do?' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's question as proof for עשו.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי acted on their view (עשו).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's question 'What shall we do with the earlier צרות?' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the worry is about the צרה herself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. The question can make sense even if בית שמאי never acted, because it concerns צרות who followed בית הלל and married others without חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It was needed only for the צרה herself. 'What shall we do' means this: those צרות who followed בית הלל, how shall we deal with them according to בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that 'What shall we do?' does not prove בית שמאי acted. The worry is about צרות who, following בית הלל, married other men without any חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית הלל a צרה is completely free and may marry anyone. According to בית שמאי she is still bound to the יבם and needed חליצה first. So making a rule requiring חליצה would cast doubt on those past marriages, even if בית שמאי themselves never did יבום with a צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for
Herself
This is what he is saying
How shall we deal with them?

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove עשו. 'What shall we do?' can refer to צרות who married others without חליצה following בית הלל, which is a problem only from בית שמאי's view.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It was needed only for the co-wife herself,
phrases.notes: The worry is about the woman's own marriage, not about children born from יבום.

phrases.english: and 'What shall we do' means this:
those co-wives of בית הלל,
phrases.notes: He means צרות who followed בית הלל and married other men without חליצה.

phrases.english: how shall we deal with them according to בית שמאי?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְצָרָה עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 3 by offering a different reading of 'What shall we do?'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this ברייתא. It does not decide whether בית שמאי acted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the worry had to be about past יבום with a צרה. It can instead be about צרות who married others without חליצה according to בית הלל.

steps.title: Why the earlier rival wives can't just do חליצה now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation. Making those women do חליצה now would make them repulsive to their husbands, and the Torah does not want that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them do חליצה? Then they would become repulsive to their husbands. And if you say, let them be repulsive, the Torah says: 'Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an obvious question on רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation: why not fix the problem by having those women do חליצה now? It explains that doing so would cause harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women followed בית הלל and married other men without חליצה. If the new proposal now required חליצה, their husbands would feel they had been living with women who were never properly permitted to them. The פסוק from משלי shows that the Torah does not want to wreck marriages this way, so this is a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them do חליצה
They would become repulsive or disgusting
And if you would say (introduces a possible objection)
Ways of pleasantness, meaning the Torah's laws do not cause needless harm

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the rejection of the proof from step 3. The worry of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes full sense even if בית שמאי never acted.

phrases.english: Let them perform חליצה —
they would become repulsive to their husbands.
And if you would say, let them be repulsive —
'Her ways are ways of pleasantness
and all her paths are peace.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the דחיה of step 4 by explaining why those women's situation is a real problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical and moral reason, backed by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Simply require חליצה now, and there is no problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Requiring חליצה now would harm existing marriages, which goes against דרכי נועם.

steps.title: Proof from רבי טרפון's wish to marry his daughter's rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי טרפון, who longed to marry his daughter's צרה. That sounds like doing יבום the way בית שמאי rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבי טרפון said: I yearn for the day my daughter's rival wife comes before me, and I will marry her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to show that בית שמאי's followers really acted on their view. רבי טרפון seems to want to do יבום with a צרת הבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בית הלל, a צרת הבת is exempt from יבום and חליצה, so marrying her through יבום would be forbidden. If רבי טרפון wanted to marry her, he must have held like בית שמאי and been ready to act on it. That would prove בית שמאי's view was put into practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source brought as proof)
I yearn or long for
The rival wife of one's daughter
And I will marry her

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Tarfon said:
I yearn: when will there come
my daughter's rival wife before me
and I will marry her!
phrases.notes: He means marrying her through יבום, which only בית שמאי allow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's followers acted on their view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי טרפון's wish to marry his daughter's צרה.

steps.title: Reread it as 'I will marry her off'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי טרפון's word so that he means marrying her off to someone else, which fits בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'and I will marry her off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by changing how one word is read. רבי טרפון wanted to marry her off to another man, not marry her himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a small change, וְאֶשָּׂאֶנָּה ('I will marry her') becomes וְאַשִּׂיאֶנָּה ('I will marry her off'). Now רבי טרפון is following בית הלל, who let a צרת הבת marry anyone without חליצה. The proof that בית שמאי acted is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
And I will marry her off to someone else

phrases.english: Say instead: 'and I will marry her off.'
phrases.notes: It is a tiny change in the word. Now he gives her to another man without חליצה, like בית הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 6 by rereading its key word.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי טרפון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depends on reading the word as 'marry her', but it can be read as 'marry her off'.

steps.title: But why would he long for something so ordinary?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: if he only meant the usual בית הלל practice, why did he say 'I yearn'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'I yearn'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading of step 7. Saying 'I yearn' only fits something special, not the normal practice everyone already follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying off a צרת הבת to another man is the common practice of בית הלל. Nobody 'longs' to do what is routine. The strong language therefore seems to point back to doing יבום like בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: But he said... (pointing to the exact words to raise a problem)

phrases.english: But he said 'I yearn'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'I will marry her off'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Longing only makes sense for something unusual. Marrying her off is ordinary, so the word 'I yearn' does not fit.

steps.title: He longed to show the הלכה is not like רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון longed for the chance to show in practice that the הלכה does not follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was to exclude the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. There was something new for רבי טרפון to show by marrying her off: that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי held that all צרות must do חליצה. By marrying off his daughter's צרה with no חליצה at all, רבי טרפון would show publicly that the הלכה follows בית הלל fully. That is why he 'yearned' for it, and the reading of step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to rule out a different opinion)
The תנא who held that all צרות must do חליצה

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
phrases.notes: He's the one who wanted all צרות to do חליצה, the idea we saw at the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and keeps the reading of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the new point in the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marrying her off is routine, so there is nothing to long for.
steps.terutzMaskana: He longed to show in practice that the הלכה is not like רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי טרפון fails. He wanted to marry off the צרה like בית הלל, to show that רבי יוחנן בן נורי is wrong.

steps.title: Proof from רבן גמליאל doing יבום with his daughter's rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story in which רבן גמליאל did יבום with his own daughter's צרה, which seems to follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There was a case with רבן גמליאל's daughter, who was married to his brother אבא. He died without children, and רבן גמליאל did יבום with her rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof, this time an actual event, to show that בית שמאי's view was put into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His daughter was one of his brother's wives, so for רבן גמליאל her co-wife was a צרת הבת. בית הלל forbid doing יבום with her, but he did it anyway. That looks like a real act following בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or actual event
And he did יבום (married his brother's widow)
Leader of the generation, a descendant of הלל

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבִתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Come and hear: There was an incident with the daughter of Rabban Gamliel
who was married to Abba, his brother,
phrases.notes: אבא is the brother's name here, so the daughter had married her own uncle.

phrases.english: and he died without children,
and Rabban Gamliel performed יבום with her rival wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבִתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רבי טרפון failed, the גמרא tries a new proof from an actual event.
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's view was carried out in practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבן גמליאל doing יבום with his daughter's צרה.

steps.title: Was רבן גמליאל really a student of בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the proof: רבן גמליאל followed בית הלל, so how could he have acted like בית שמאי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think so? Was רבן גמליאל one of the students of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof right away. It is setting up a different way to understand the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל came from the family of הלל and followed בית הלל. It makes no sense that he would do יבום with a צרת הבת like בית שמאי. So the story must have some other explanation, which the גמרא will give next.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (shows the idea is hard to accept)
Students or followers of בית שמאי

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not say the story is false. It only says the story cannot mean רבן גמליאל was following בית שמאי, so it must be explained another way.

phrases.english: And can you really understand it that way?

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הוּא?
phrases.english: Was Rabban Gamliel one of the students of Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 10 and prepares a new explanation of the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבן גמליאל acted like בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל followed בית הלל, so he would not have done יבום with a צרת הבת like בית שמאי.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's daughter was an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: The case is different, because רבן גמליאל's daughter was an אילונית. Her marriage did not count, so the other wife was not a forbidden צרה even according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case of רבן גמליאל's daughter is different, because she was an אילונית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11. רבן גמליאל did not follow בית שמאי here. His daughter was an אילונית, and that is why the יבום was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if the forbidden relative was an אילונית, her צרה is permitted, because the marriage to the אילונית was a mistaken marriage. So the other wife never became a צרת ערוה. That means even בית הלל would allow her יבום, and the proof that anyone acted like בית שמאי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. This case is unusual and cannot be used as a proof.
A woman who never developed physically and cannot have children. A marriage to her made without knowing this is a mistaken marriage.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׁאנֵי בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabban Gamliel's daughter is different,
for she was an aylonit.
phrases.notes: Her marriage to רבן גמליאל's brother did not really count, so the other wife was not her צרה in the legal sense.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שָׁאנֵי בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by showing that this case is a special exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני): a special fact removes it from the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל did יבום with a real צרת ערוה, which is the practice of בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: His daughter was an אילונית, so the other wife was not a forbidden צרה at all, and בית הלל would also allow the יבום.

steps.title: The ברייתא suggests the תנא קמא disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says 'אחרים say she was an אילונית.' This implies that the תנא קמא held she was not, so he cannot use this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the ברייתא teaches, 'Others say רבן גמליאל's daughter was an אילונית,' it follows that the first תנא holds she was not an אילונית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 12. It points to the wording of the ברייתא itself, where only 'others' say she was an אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אילונית fact were agreed by everyone, why would the ברייתא give it in the name of a separate group? This suggests the תנא קמא denied it. If so, his version of the story still shows רבן גמליאל acting like בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא.
'Others say': a second opinion given in the same source.
By implication: we can learn this from what was said.
The first תנא, whose opinion opens the ברייתא.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
Others say

phrases.aramaic: בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַיְלוֹנִית הָיְתָה,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel's daughter was an aylonit,
it follows that the first tanna holds
she was not an aylonit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the אילונית answer of step 12, based on how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that רבן גמליאל's daughter was an אילונית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the ברייתא gives the אילונית fact only in the name of 'others,' it implies that the תנא קמא disagrees. That brings the בית שמאי problem back according to him.

steps.title: They disagree about whether he knew
steps.stepSummary: Both תנאים agree she was an אילונית. They argue about a general rule: does it matter whether the husband knew of her condition when he married her?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether he knew about her or did not know about her: that is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 13. The two תנאים do not argue about the fact. They argue about a rule connected to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband knew she was an אילונית and married her anyway, it is not a mistaken marriage, and her צרה may be forbidden. If he did not know, the marriage was a mistake and her צרה is permitted. The 'others' mention the אילונית fact because, according to their view of this rule, it is the deciding point. It does not mean the תנא קמא denies the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: He knew about her, meaning the husband was aware she was an אילונית.
There is a difference between them. This introduces the real point of disagreement.

phrases.english: He knew about her or did not know about her,
phrases.notes: He means: did the husband know she was an אילונית before he married her?

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִכִּיר בָּהּ וְלֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by moving the disagreement from the fact to a legal rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the disagreement: the תנאים argue about a rule (איכא בינייהו), not about the facts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא denies that the daughter was an אילונית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees she was an אילונית. They argue only about whether the husband's knowing about her condition changes the law.

steps.title: Second answer: married and later divorced
steps.stepSummary: Another way to explain the disagreement: the תנאים argue about a case where the brother married the daughter and later divorced her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: the difference between them is a case where he married her and in the end divorced her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to explain what the two תנאים argue about. Both still agree she was an אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא discussed whether a wife stays a צרה if the forbidden relative was divorced before the husband died. One תנא may hold that the divorce alone already permits the other wife, so he does not need the אילונית reason. The 'others' hold she would still be a צרה, so they point to the אילונית fact.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: this introduces another possible answer.
He married her.
In the end, he divorced her.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
married and ultimately divorced
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier question: is she still a צרה if the forbidden relative was divorced before the brother died?

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כָּנַס וּלְבַסּוֹף גֵּירַשׁ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'others' clause shows that the תנא קמא denies she was an אילונית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree she was an אילונית. They argue about whether a forbidden relative who was married and then divorced still makes the other wife a צרה.

steps.title: Third answer: a condition in a marriage
steps.stepSummary: A third way to explain the disagreement: the תנאים argue whether a marriage made with a condition stays conditional even after the couple lived together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: the difference between them is whether a condition still stands once the couple has lived together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third possible explanation of the disagreement between the two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא may hold that the condition stays in force even after they lived together. Since it was not met, the daughter was never married to the brother, so there is no need for the אילונית reason. The 'others' hold that living together cancels the condition, so the only reason left is that she was an אילונית. Either way, the story does not prove that רבן גמליאל acted like בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition attached to a marriage.
Living together as husband and wife.

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רבן גמליאל's daughter does not prove that anyone acted like בית שמאי. She was an אילונית, so the other wife was never a forbidden צרה. The 'others' clause in the ברייתא only reflects a disagreement about a related rule: whether he knew, whether there was a divorce first, or whether a condition stays after living together.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
there is a condition in sexual relations
phrases.notes: He means: if a man married on a condition and then lived with her, does the condition still count?

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא יֵשׁ תְּנַאי בְּבִיאָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, independent answer to the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא denies the אילונית fact and holds that רבן גמליאל did יבום with a real צרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא may permit the יבום because an unmet condition cancelled the marriage. The 'others' need the אילונית reason because, in their view, living together cancels the condition.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא tithed an אתרוג according to both opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges the claim that בית שמאי did not act on their opinion. He cites the story of רבי עקיבא, who tithed an אתרוג picked on א׳ בשבט twice, once following בית שמאי and once following בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא raised an objection: There was a story with רבי עקיבא. He picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט and took off two different tithes from it. One tithe followed בית שמאי, and one followed בית הלל. So we see that people did act according to בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא brings a story to challenge the idea that nobody acted according to בית שמאי. רבי עקיבא, a great חכם, seems to have done exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that the new year for trees is א׳ בשבט, and בית הלל hold it is ט״ו בשבט. An אתרוג picked on א׳ בשבט falls in the new year for בית שמאי but in the old year for בית הלל, and each year may need a different tithe. Since רבי עקיבא took both tithes, he seems to be treating בית שמאי's opinion as something to act on.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from an earlier source
Citron fruit; its tithing year is set by when it is picked
Tithes, such as מעשר שני and מעשר עני
New year for trees: א׳ בשבט for בית שמאי, ט״ו בשבט for בית הלל
They acted, meaning בית שמאי actually acted on their own ruling

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא did not take two tithes because he wanted extra. He took them because each opinion puts this אתרוג in a different year, and different years need different tithes.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya raised an objection:
There was an incident with Rabbi Akiva
who picked an etrog on the first of Shevat,
and he took two tithes from it.
phrases.notes: Different years of the seven-year cycle need different tithes, so he took off the tithe for each of the two possible years.

phrases.english: One according to the words of Beit Shammai,
and one according to the words of Beit Hillel.
Learn from this: they did act!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier steps rejected the attempted proof from רבן גמליאל's daughter. Now רב משרשיא brings a new source on the same question of whether בית שמאי acted on their view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that בית שמאי did not act on their own rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא, a major חכם, took a tithe based on בית שמאי's date for the new year for trees. That looks like acting on בית שמאי's opinion.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא was unsure what בית הלל held
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא was really trying to follow בית הלל. He was unsure whether their new year for trees was א׳ בשבט or ט״ו בשבט, so he tithed both ways to be safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא was unsure about what he had learned. He did not know whether בית הלל said the first of שבט or the fifteenth of שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב משרשיא by explaining why רבי עקיבא tithed twice. He was not following בית שמאי at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double tithe was not 'one for בית שמאי and one for בית הלל.' It came from a doubt about what בית הלל themselves said. So this story does not prove that anyone acted according to בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: His learning, the tradition he received from his teachers
He was in doubt
Was said

steps.whatToRemember: Acting out of doubt about בית הלל's opinion is not the same as following בית שמאי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva was unsure of his tradition,
and he did not know whether Beit Hillel
had said the first of Shevat,
or had said the fifteenth of Shevat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי עקיבא's אתרוג in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the reason behind the action: a doubt within בית הלל, not following בית שמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two tithes were one for בית שמאי and one for בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both tithes were about doubt over בית הלל's own date, so there is no proof that anyone acted according to בית שמאי.

steps.title: שמאי הזקן built a סוכה over a newborn
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a different story. שמאי הזקן broke open the plaster roof and put סכך over the bed of his newborn grandson, acting on his own view that even a tiny baby must sit in a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא raised an objection: There was a story in which the daughter-in-law of שמאי הזקן gave birth. He broke away the plaster of the roof and put סכך over the bed for the baby. So we see that they did act on בית שמאי's view!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא brings a second story to show that בית שמאי acted on their own opinion. This time it is שמאי himself, acting in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל do not require a small baby to sit in a סוכה, but שמאי did. By making a סוכה for a newborn, שמאי seems to be openly acting on his own ruling. That seems to prove עשו.

keyTerms.meaning: Shammai the Elder, head of בית שמאי
His daughter-in-law
The plaster layer of a roof
He covered it with סכך, the roofing of a סוכה
A minor, here a newborn baby

phrases.english: Mar Zutra raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וְיָלְדָה כַּלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן,
phrases.english: There was an incident: the daughter-in-law of Shammai the Elder gave birth,
and he broke away the plaster of the roof

phrases.aramaic: וְסִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה בִּשְׁבִיל קָטָן.
phrases.english: and put sukkah-covering over the bed for the baby.
Learn from this: they did act!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אתרוג proof is answered, a new and separate proof is brought for the same claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that בית שמאי did not act on their own rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמאי openly built a סוכה for a newborn, which only his own opinion requires. That shows him acting on בית שמאי's view.

steps.title: Onlookers would think he just wanted fresh air
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is no proof. Someone seeing a hole opened in the roof would assume שמאי did it to let in more air, not to follow a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different. Someone who sees it would say he is doing it to let in more air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers מר זוטרא's challenge. It explains that שמאי's action did not look like acting on a ruling of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is about publicly acting on a ruling against בית הלל. Opening a roof over a baby looks like an ordinary practical step, like getting fresh air, so nobody watching would see a statement of הלכה. That is why this story does not count as עשו.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who sees it, an onlooker
To add more air
He is doing it

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs are answered. רבי עקיבא acted out of doubt about בית הלל, and שמאי's act looked like an everyday action, so neither shows open action on בית שמאי's rulings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that what matters is how an act looks to others. A private-looking or ordinary action is not treated as publicly following a ruling.

phrases.english: There, someone who sees it would say
that he is doing it to let in more air.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, הָרוֹאֶה אוֹמֵר לְאַפּוֹשֵׁי אֲוִיר קָעָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case by how the act looks to an observer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making a סוכה for a baby is an open act following בית שמאי's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Onlookers would see it as just letting in air, so it is not considered acting publicly on בית שמאי's view.

steps.title: בית שמאי widened the hole in the trough of יהוא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges the claim that בית שמאי did not act on their view. He tells how בית שמאי widened the hole connecting the trough of יהוא to a מקוה, because they hold the opening must cover most of the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: There was a story about the trough of יהוא in ירושלים. It had a hole connecting it to a מקוה, and all the purifications in ירושלים were done in it. בית שמאי sent people and widened the hole, because בית שמאי say the connection does not count until most of the wall is broken open.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא brings a new story to show that בית שמאי did act on their opinion. They physically widened the hole in a trough that everyone in ירושלים was using for purification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trough on its own cannot purify, but it can if it is joined to a real מקוה. The whole city treated the existing hole as enough. בית שמאי disagreed and enlarged it, which looks like acting on their own ruling in public.

keyTerms.meaning: A stone water trough
A ritual bath used for purification
Purifications; things made pure by dipping them
Until most of it is broken open

phrases.english: Mar Zutra raised an objection:
There was an incident with the trough of Yehu
that was in Jerusalem,
and it had a hole opening into the mikveh,
and all the purifications that were in Jerusalem
were done in it.
And Beit Shammai sent people and widened it,
because Beit Shammai say:
it does not count until most of it is broken open,
phrases.notes: He means most of the wall between the trough and the מקוה has to be open.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the סוכה story was pushed aside in step 20, מר זוטרא brings a second story to make the same challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית שמאי did not act on their own opinions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי publicly changed a trough the whole city used, to fit their own stricter rule about joining it to a מקוה.

steps.title: בית הלל accept a small hole, so בית שמאי acted against them
steps.stepSummary: The challenge quotes a משנה showing that a hole the size of a wineskin's tube is enough to join מקואות. That is בית הלל's view, so בית שמאי's widening shows they acted on their own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: joining מקואות needs a hole like the tube of a wineskin, in its thickness and its open space, big enough for two fingers to turn around in it. Learn from this that בית שמאי acted on their view!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge finishes by showing how far apart the two views are. בית הלל accept a small hole, so widening it could only be because of בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a small, exact size for the hole. The trough's hole was already enough by that standard, and that is why the city used it. Since בית שמאי still widened it, the challenge concludes they acted on their own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Joining ritual baths together through an opening
The tube or spout of a leather wineskin
Turning around in their place
Learn from this

phrases.english: And we learned: joining ritual baths
is done with an opening like the tube of a wineskin
in its thickness and its open space,
big enough for two fingers to turn around in place.
Learn from this that they acted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes מר זוטרא's challenge by giving בית הלל's smaller size and drawing the conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי acted on their own opinion
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on עירוב מקואות shows that בית הלל accept a small hole, so widening it only makes sense by בית שמאי's rule.

steps.title: The answer begins: "There…"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer מר זוטרא by pointing to the trough case with the word "there." The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There…
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening word of the גמרא's answer. It is setting up the next move, which will explain why the trough story does not prove that בית שמאי acted against בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הָתָם ("there") tells us the גמרא is about to show that the trough case is special. Just like the סוכה story in step 20, it will find a way to read the story so it is not a true proof.

keyTerms.meaning: There; in that case (opens an answer that sets one case apart)

phrases.english: There

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the reply to מר זוטרא's challenge in steps 21-22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting the case apart (the full answer continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trough story shows that בית שמאי acted on their own ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full answer comes on the next amud. Here the גמרא is only starting to explain why the trough case is different.
